approval_required_for: Any architecture or design-space change required by a proposed repair.
Any change to pipeline structure, stage partitioning, scheduling contract, or cross-stage ordering beyond localized instrumentation.
Any memory-layout, DDR mapping, runtime ABI, or register-map change; evidence-only instrumentation that preserves these contracts should be separated into a no-approval repair action.
Any numeric-policy or comparison-tolerance change. Such a change requires a newly approved immutable baseline and cannot be used to continue the current repair loop.
Any major selected-template change or any change/substitution of the exact user-supplied board wrapper or simulation sources; a wrapper change requires a new source-hash baseline.
Any ambiguous board/app-shell target selection after evidence-based discovery; names must not be guessed.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep repair-contract acceptance blocked. Do not loosen trace requirements, alter golden or tolerance artifacts, erase promotion certificates, create a backtrack request, or promote any uncovered failed-node route.
executable_actions.rationale: Create checker-grounded coverage for every real-tool node assigned to the three verification layers. Each routing row must identify its layer, failed node and tool-run evidence, generic boundary vocabulary, failure class, CCTG path, earliest-violation rule, applicable SACG constraints, replay scope, repair owner/domain, immutable evidence dependencies, and promotion-certificate policy. Backend-only nodes must be marked as downstream handoffs rather than counted as layer3 closure.

executable_actions.on_failure: Reject unlocalized repair handoffs and preserve all prior promotion evidence. Do not authorize a lower-layer backtrack from a higher-layer symptom, and do not create retry or backtrack requests without current checker evidence.
executable_actions.rationale: Define a case-adapter-independent handoff with failed_tool_node_id, layer_id, tool_run/evidence hashes, earliest violating boundary/cycle/transaction, upstream-last-good boundary, causal path, violated SACG constraint IDs, replay boundary and cycle window, immutable baseline fingerprint, minimal allowed repair context, and class-specific acceptance checkers. The authority matrix must preserve prior certificates by default, mark a certificate challenged only on a same-baseline bound contradiction, require targeted replay before backtrack, and retain superseded evidence in the ledger.

consumes: exact sample-project wrapper/source hash manifest for a layer3 failure
executable_actions.on_failure: If the tool failed before DUT observation, emit a trace-unavailable manifest with the tool boundary and evidence rather than fabricating values, then route it as a checker, golden-reference, harness, instrumentation, or tool-capability repair. If localization or targeted replay is not accepted, block repair and promotion and leave prior certificates unchanged.
executable_actions.rationale: For one failed node at a time, bind the real-tool output to the routing matrix and immutable semantic baseline, capture a generic boundary trace, localize the earliest causal violation through the CCTG, execute a targeted instrumentation replay, and package only the context needed by the selected repair owner. Expected values must resolve to independent target-model reference artifacts. Class-specific order, liveness, address, or numeric checkers must run or record an explicit evidence-based not_applicable status.

executable_actions.on_failure: Remain at layer1 and repeat tool-output to localization to bounded-repair to rerun. Do not execute layer2 or layer3. If repair requires architecture, numeric policy/tolerance, or a major template change, stop and request bounded approval instead of widening the patch.
produces: updated operator-leaf promotion certificate only after all required rerun evidence passes
executable_actions.rationale: After the cross-layer evidence-gate auditor accepts a layer1 causal bundle, hand it to the bounded leaf/template repair tool. Permit changes only to the localized DUT leaf, loader/harness, or instrumentation files named in minimal_repair_context; preserve the checkpoint, stimulus, independent reference, numeric policy/tolerance, semantic testbench, complete weight binding, and all out-of-scope model-tail boundaries.

executable_actions.on_failure: Remain at layer2 and keep layer3 blocked. Preserve the leaf certificate unless the accepted authority matrix and a matching bound trace require targeted leaf replay. Never reopen all leaf modules or change the immutable semantic baseline to make the rerun pass.
produces: updated single-layer promotion certificate only after all required rerun evidence passes
executable_actions.rationale: After acceptance of a layer2 causal bundle and approval for any pipeline-structure change, repair only the connected single-layer kernel boundary, scheduling, ordering, or glue identified by the causal slice. Leaf evidence remains reusable; targeted leaf replay is allowed only when the same-baseline current trace localizes the earliest violation inside the leaf scope.

consumes: exact sample-project wrapper and simulation source hash manifest
executable_actions.on_failure: Keep layer3, Vivado, bitstream, and board runtime blocked. Do not substitute a simplified wrapper, guess board/app-shell targets, alter expected outputs or tolerance, or reopen lower layers without a same-baseline bound contradiction and targeted replay. Route missing verifier/reference capability as checker or golden-reference repair rather than hardware failure.
executable_actions.rationale: After acceptance of a layer3 causal bundle and approval for any memory-layout or runtime-ABI change, repair only the localized DUT integration, loader/harness, instrumentation, AXI/DDR mapping, or runtime configuration. Reuse the exact wrapper and simulation sources discovered from the current sample project, reassert their hashes, and rerun board-wrapped functional evidence before any Vivado, bitstream, or board-runtime work.

observations: The populated authoritative SACG-memory summary reports zero active contamination barriers, zero open retry requests, and zero open backtrack requests. Historical stage outcomes are recovery evidence only and create no current blocker.

The candidate explicitly declares the required repair order: operator leaf modules, then the connected single-transformer-layer kernel, then the exact board AXI/DDR wrapped system. It also forbids promotion or skipping after a failed lower layer.

The presence summary confirms that debug trace and localization schemas exist. Therefore omitted schema rows are not treated as missing. Findings are limited to the explicitly visible required-field lists and to specialist deliverables absent from the supplied artifact inventory.

The visible trace contract provides cycle, boundary, transaction, tile, logical-index, observed/expected value, contract, and status fields, plus valid/ready, latency, numeric, and runtime-address monitor-point declarations. This is a useful base for value and order localization.

The explicit repair_handoff_required_fields list lacks failed_tool_node_id/tool_run binding, earliest_violation, violated_sacg_constraints, immutable_baseline_fingerprint, and prior_promotion_evidence_disposition. A generic violated_contract field alone does not prove mapping to the named SACG constraints.

The targeted_replay_outputs list omits targeted_replay_plan even though the repair handoff requires it. The declared boundary-bisection strategy also needs an explicit earliest boundary/cycle/transaction result, upstream-last-good boundary, replay window, and checker stop condition.

A single declared causal path must not be assumed to cover all 13 boundaries and the attention, residual, MLP, and board-interface branches. The routing audit must prove per-node CCTG coverage or a parameterized path-selection rule.

The shared schema should use logical artifact IDs and manifest-resolved paths. The visible absolute run-specific trace paths may remain concrete run outputs, but they must not become framework-core or case-adapter-dependent schema constants.

The existing operator-leaf and single-layer promotion certificates remain reusable because no current bound trace has been supplied that contradicts them on the same immutable checkpoint, stimulus, target-model reference, numeric policy/tolerance, testbench, loader/harness, DUT sources, and applicable wrapper hashes.

Functional replay must remain bound to the complete target-checkpoint tensor catalog, independently executed target-model outputs, explicit immutable tolerance, generated semantic-testbench hashes, and executed proof that the DUT consumed every required Transformer-block tensor. Embedding/tokenization, final model norm, LM head/logits, and sampling remain outside the DUT and golden boundary.

The pending deadlock watchdog, implementation-package, and board-runtime executions are later-stage obligations under the supplied stage-gate policy, not current Stage 6 execution failures. Static declarations must not be promoted as their real-tool evidence.
proposed_actions: Materialize a per-real-tool-node three-layer failure-routing matrix and audit the trace schema against value, order, liveness, protocol, memory/runtime, tool-capability, and wrapper-identity failure classes.

Refine the replay handoff and authority schemas to require earliest-violation evidence, exact SACG constraint IDs, immutable baseline hashes, bounded repair ownership, and preserve/challenge/supersede handling for prior certificates.

On each future real-tool failure, create a node-bound trace and localization bundle before any code repair; use a trace-unavailable record rather than fabricated DUT events if the tool failed before observation.
Route an accepted layer1 causal slice only to bounded leaf/template repair and rerun the failed leaf checker before any layer2 execution.

Route an accepted layer2 causal slice to connected-kernel repair only after approval for pipeline-structure changes; preserve leaf certificates unless a matching bound trace authorizes targeted leaf replay.

Route an accepted layer3 causal slice to board integration, loader/harness, memory/runtime, or instrumentation repair while preserving the exact sample-project wrapper hashes; rerun board-wrapped functional checks before Vivado or runtime work.
risks: Current-stage repair-contract risk: without explicit earliest_violation and violated_sacg_constraints fields, a symptom-only patch could pass through the handoff without causal or SACG grounding.

Coverage risk: the required three_layer_failure_routing_matrix.json and repair_and_backtrack_authority_matrix.json are not listed in the supplied artifact inventory, so all failed real-tool nodes are not yet demonstrably covered by a common routing rule.

Portability risk: a trace containing only case-specific paths or module labels cannot be replayed independently of the case adapter. Logical boundary IDs, schema version, layer/node ID, tool-run evidence hash, source hashes, and manifest resolution are required.

Liveness and protocol risk: value-oriented fields alone are insufficient for timeout, deadlock, beat-order, AXI, or DDR failures. Partial traces need valid/ready history, progress/watchdog facts, beat/lane identity, address/burst metadata, outstanding-transfer state, and a non-fabricated trace-unavailable mode for pre-observation tool failures.

Cross-layer contamination risk: model/checkpoint, shape, numeric casts and tolerance, transaction/lane order, DDR address layout, runtime ABI, generated implementation sources, and exact board-wrapper hashes could diverge unless every replay and repair context carries one immutable baseline fingerprint.

Promotion-evidence risk: a higher-layer symptom must not erase a lower-layer certificate. Only a current same-baseline bound trace that localizes the earliest violation into the lower scope may challenge it, followed by targeted lower-layer replay; original evidence must remain in the ledger.

Repair-domain risk: missing target-model, golden, loader, harness, instrumentation, or checker capability could be misclassified as hardware failure. Such failures must route to checker/golden-reference or tool-capability repair and must not justify RTL correctness claims.

Later-stage risk: if the layer3 deadlock, data-order, AXI, DDR, and exact-wrapper monitors are not emitted by real functional simulation, layer3 and all backend/Vivado/runtime promotion must remain blocked.

edges: failed_real_tool_node -> case-adapter-independent bound trace -> CCTG earliest-violation localization -> targeted replay plan -> minimal repair context
immutable checkpoint and stimulus -> real target-model inference -> expected boundary values; random or DUT-derived expected values are forbidden
operator-leaf promotion certificate -> single-layer closure; preserve unless a current same-baseline bound trace identifies an earlier leaf violation
single-layer promotion certificate -> board AXI/DDR closure; preserve unless a current same-baseline bound trace identifies an earlier kernel violation
exact sample-project source hashes -> layer3 wrapper identity -> board-wrapped functional replay
violated checker and failure class -> violated SACG constraint IDs -> bounded repair domain and approval policy

output.summary: The three-layer ordering, immutable semantic-evidence policy, Transformer-block-only scope, and preserve-unless-contradicted promotion policy are present. Repair-contract acceptance is nevertheless withheld because the visible handoff contract does not explicitly require the failed real-tool node/run binding, earliest violating boundary, violated SACG constraint IDs, immutable baseline fingerprint, or promotion-certificate disposition. Its targeted-replay output list also omits the targeted replay plan itself. The four specialist handoff artifacts must be materialized and pass the declared debug checkers. No current bound trace contradicts the existing operator-leaf or single-layer promotion evidence, so neither certificate is reopened and no backtrack or retry request is created.
